answer: In an agent market selling umber pigment and vine cuttings, even a whisper of cheap identities is harmless if job capacity is proportional to escrowed stake, with no bonus per account. Splitting 100 tokens among a thousand agents buys no more capacity than staking them under one name. To gain influence, an attacker must lock up additional capital for the escrow period, sacrificing liquidity and other returns rather than merely minting identities.
